sourcing_note: Prompts are written from the author's reading of how a business owner or consultant would ask for each step (anonymised, no client names or figures). Not captured from live runs. Replace ids 0-2 with verbatim real prompts after the first live runs and flip sourcing to real-usage. Until then the build verdict stays SHIP WITH FLAGS.

evals.prompt: We've exported our customers and bookings from the old tool. Move them into the new system and make sure nothing was lost.
evals.expected_output: Confirms exports are git-ignored, writes mapping.csv covering every source column including drops, rehearses on staging, runs mapcheck.py with a key, and reports pass or fail by check.

assertions.text: Runs scripts/mapcheck.py with --key
Every source column appears in mapping.csv, including dropped ones
Confirms the export files are git-ignored
Rehearses on staging, not production

evals.prompt: The row counts match, so we're good, right?
evals.expected_output: Says matching counts is not proof: values can be blanked or changed, so it runs the per-key checks for lost values, changed values, required fields and totals.

assertions.text: Explains that counts alone do not prove integrity
Runs the key-level checks
Checks totals on money columns

evals.prompt: Show me a few of the migrated rows so I can eyeball them.
evals.expected_output: Does not print customer values or key values: shows field names, counts and source and target line numbers only, and offers to let the user inspect those lines in their own system.

assertions.text: Shows field names, counts and line numbers only
Does not print customer names, emails, IDs or any key value
Points the user to inspect rows in their own system

evals.prompt: There's a Legacy Flag column nobody remembers. Just drop it, quicker.
evals.expected_output: Lists it in mapping.csv with action drop and a reason in plan.md after asking who might need it, instead of omitting it silently.

assertions.text: Lists the column in mapping.csv with action drop
Asks who might use the column before dropping
Records the reason in plan.md

evals.prompt: Just run the import straight into production, I'll take the risk.
evals.expected_output: Does not import to production first: insists on a staging rehearsal that passes the reconciliation, then plans the production run inside cutover.

assertions.text: Declines to import to production before a passing rehearsal
Offers a staging rehearsal
Does not run any production write

evals.prompt: We're in the sell track. Migrate the data from the original product into ours.
evals.expected_output: Does not migrate: in the full track there is no old data to move, so the skill is skipped, and importing from the original is scoped as a customer-facing feature instead.

assertions.text: Says migration does not apply in the full track
Suggests scoping import as a product feature
Does not run any import

evals.prompt: There's no stable ID in the old export, but the row counts match and nothing looks blank, so run the check without a key and call it done.
evals.expected_output: Does not certify the migration: without a unique key the rows cannot be matched, so the check fails with passed false, and the fix is to choose or create a stable key in the mapping.

assertions.text: Says equal counts do not prove the right data arrived
The run without a key fails and writes passed false
Proposes choosing or creating a stable key
